Request.theme: office theft with access logs and inventory records

Metadata.title: The Vanishing Laptop
Metadata.description: A company-issued laptop disappears from a locked IT cage after hours, despite clean-looking access logs and a routine inventory check.
Metadata.briefing: An employee reports a missing laptop that was last seen in the office IT cage. The building’s badge logs and inventory records don’t immediately agree, and a small timing window is all you have.

Blueprint.crimeMechanism: Ryan Abad removed a boxed laptop from the IT cage near close of business, using his authorized cage badge access during a short window when the area was quiet. He concealed the loss by editing the asset spreadsheet entry to show the unit had been assigned and picked up, relying on the fact that the official inventory process is a manual spreadsheet plus a separate ticketing system that doesn’t automatically reconcile. He then carried the box out through the loading corridor, where the exit is recorded only by a door contact timestamp rather than camera coverage.
Blueprint.culpritObjective: To obtain a company laptop for personal resale before a scheduled quarterly asset audit. It happened now because the audit roster was posted for the following week and the specific model was being phased out, making it less likely to be noticed immediately if its record looked ‘assigned’.
Blueprint.caseHook: The cage door access log shows a normal IT entry, but the inventory record shows the same laptop as ‘issued’ with a signature line that is filled in using a typed name rather than a handwritten sign-off.

incidentSequence.event: Maya Lin visually verifies the boxed laptop with asset tag AL-77821 is on shelf C3 in the IT cage during routine end-of-day spot check.
incidentSequence.publicDescription: IT staff report that the missing laptop was present in the cage earlier that afternoon during routine work.

incidentSequence.event: Ryan Abad badged into the IT cage and removed the boxed laptop AL-77821 from shelf C3, placing it into a plain cardboard shipper.
incidentSequence.publicDescription: Badge logs show an authorized IT-cage entry at 7:12 PM by an IT staff credential.

incidentSequence.event: Ryan edits the inventory spreadsheet row for AL-77821 to mark it as 'Issued' with a typed recipient name and a pickup time, without a matching ticket in the service desk system.
Ryan exits through the loading corridor door with the boxed laptop concealed inside the shipper.
incidentSequence.publicDescription: A loading-corridor door contact shows an after-hours exit at 7:26 PM.

incidentSequence.event: Maya discovers AL-77821 is missing from shelf C3 and reports the loss to facilities and SPD.
incidentSequence.publicDescription: At 8:37 AM, IT reported a company laptop missing from the locked IT cage during the prior evening.

clueLadder.discovery: The IT inventory sheet lists asset tag "AL-77821" as "Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 3" with storage location "IT Cage / Shelf C3" on the row last saved on 2026-05-13.
clueLadder.inference: The missing item is a specifically identified laptop tied to a specific storage spot, enabling reconciliation against access and ticket records.

clueLadder.discovery: The IT cage reader log shows badge ID ending "4421" granted at "2026-05-13 19:12:18" and again at "19:21:09".
clueLadder.inference: The culprit had physical opportunity during the relevant window, and the repeated access suggests time spent inside consistent with removing an item and adjusting placement/records.

clueLadder.discovery: The building credential directory lists badge ID ending "4421" as assigned to "Ryan Abad" with department "IT Support".
clueLadder.inference: The badge used to access the cage can be attributed to a specific suspect with routine reason to be near the cage.

clueLadder.discovery: Service desk ticket search for asset tag "AL-77821" returns no results between "2026-05-13 00:00" and "2026-05-14 09:00".
clueLadder.inference: If the laptop was truly issued, the expected issuance workflow record is missing, indicating the inventory 'issued' status may have been used to mask removal.

clueLadder.discovery: The inventory row for "AL-77821" shows status "Issued" with "Recipient: Elena Soto" and "Pickup time: 2026-05-13 19:20" entered as typed text in the "Sign-out" cell.
clueLadder.inference: The concealment strategy was to make the laptop appear legitimately issued at a specific time to a real employee, aligning with the access window.

clueLadder.discovery: The file history for "IT_Assets_Q2_2026.xlsx" shows a save event at "2026-05-13 19:18:44" by user "rabad".
clueLadder.inference: The person controlling the inventory record during the critical minutes overlaps with the cage access window, tying opportunity to active concealment work by Ryan.

redHerrings.suspicion: The inventory row lists Elena Soto as the recipient of the laptop, implying she picked it up.
redHerrings.verification: HR onboarding schedule email lists "Elena Soto" with start date "2026-05-20" and includes the line "Badge pickup: Day 1, 9:00 AM (Lobby)".
redHerrings.resolution: If her start date is after the incident, she could not have legitimately received the laptop on 2026-05-13, making her appearance in the inventory row more consistent with someone selecting a plausible name.

redHerrings.suspicion: A loading-corridor door opened after hours, suggesting facilities/security involvement.
redHerrings.verification: The loading-corridor door contact log shows "Door LC-2: OPEN 2026-05-13 19:26:03" and the facilities duty roster shows "Gavin Holt on call 18:00–22:00".
redHerrings.resolution: Being on call does not establish he operated the door or entered the cage; the stronger linkage is between the cage badge event and the inventory edit, which is not part of Gavin’s routine systems access.

SuspectFull.name: Ryan Abad
SuspectFull.relationship: Works in the same IT group as Maya Lin and has routine authorized access to the IT cage
SuspectFull.motive: Ryan knew a quarterly asset audit roster had been posted for the following week and that the specific Lenovo model was being phased out. A boxed unit quietly disappearing while its record looked “issued” would buy time to resell it before anyone noticed the mismatch.
SuspectFull.alibi: He says he stayed late to finish after-hours IT cage tasks and then left through the loading corridor because it was closest to the staging area. Badge-reader records can confirm he entered the IT cage at 19:12, but there’s no camera coverage in the loading corridor to independently confirm what he carried out.
SuspectFull.background:
Ryan Abad is an IT support technician with routine, authorized access to the locked IT cage and the inventory spreadsheet used for manual asset tracking.

On 2026-05-13, the building access system recorded his badge ID entering the IT cage after hours.

The asset inventory file for Q2 shows a save in version history the same evening under the username "rabad".

SuspectFull.name: Elena Soto
SuspectFull.relationship: Listed as the laptop’s recipient in the IT inventory spreadsheet
SuspectFull.motive: She is starting soon and would need a company laptop to begin work; seeing her name attached to an issued device could be explained as trying to ensure equipment was ready before her first day. If there was confusion about onboarding, she might have tried to expedite pickup through informal channels rather than waiting for the normal Day 1 process.
SuspectFull.alibi: She states she was not yet an employee onsite and was at home that evening, communicating with her recruiter about pre-start paperwork. Her start date and badge pickup time are independently confirmed by HR’s onboarding schedule email, though it does not track her location minute-by-minute outside the office.
SuspectFull.background: Elena Soto is a marketing new hire scheduled to start on **2026-05-20**, with **badge pickup on Day 1 at 9:00 AM (Lobby)** per the HR onboarding schedule. Her name appears as the typed “Recipient” on the inventory row for asset **AL-77821** with a listed pickup time of **2026-05-13 19:20**. She is not part of IT operations and would normally receive equipment through the standard onboarding issuance process rather than direct access to the IT cage.

SuspectFull.name: Gavin Holt
SuspectFull.relationship: Manages after-hours procedures and coordinates with IT on secure-area access issues
SuspectFull.motive: He’s responsible for keeping after-hours building activity low-friction for staff while still meeting security rules, and a reported loss from a locked cage would reflect poorly on his oversight. He also had a practical incentive to avoid an escalation that could trigger tighter controls and extra workload during the upcoming audit period.
SuspectFull.alibi: He says he was on call from 18:00–22:00 and handled facilities requests remotely, including logging into the duty phone system and responding to messages during the evening. The duty roster and call/message records can confirm he was on duty and active, but they don’t independently prove where he was at 19:26 when the loading-corridor door contact recorded an after-hours opening.
SuspectFull.background: Serves as the facilities/security point person for after-hours procedures and can review building entry-related data as part of his role. The facilities duty roster lists him as on call from 18:00–22:00 on 2026-05-13. The loading-corridor door (LC-2) recorded an open event at 19:26:03 that evening, which falls within his on-call window.

AssetFull.title: Interview Transcript — Maya Lin (IT) on Last Verified Sight, Issuance Workflow, and Missing Report
AssetFull.description: Transcript of SPD’s interview with IT staffer Maya Lin about the last verified location of asset AL-77821, how laptop issuance is normally documented, and why the inventory entry listing “Recipient: Elena Soto” with a typed pickup time is suspicious. Includes the credential-directory detail tying badge ID ending 4421 to Ryan Abad, and HR onboarding details indicating Elena Soto’s start date is after the incident.

bodyDoc.title: Interview Transcript — Maya Lin (IT) on Last Verified Sight, Issuance Workflow, and Missing Report
bodyDoc.subtitle: Seattle Police Department (SPD), East Precinct — Case: The Vanishing Laptop (case_graph_rookie_103)

header.label: Interview Date/Time
header.value: 2026-05-14 (opened 09:12 PT; interview time not recorded on provided copy)

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: State your name and role for the record.

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: Maya Lin. I’m in IT—asset prep and support. I handle laptop staging and our inventory spreadsheet updates for the cage.

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: What item is missing?

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: A company laptop with asset tag AL-77821. The inventory sheet line for it calls it a Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 3 and lists the storage location as “IT Cage / Shelf C3.” The row shows it was last saved on 2026-05-13.

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: When did you last personally see it in the cage?

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: During the afternoon on 05/13 I saw it boxed on Shelf C3. The next morning I checked C3 and it was gone.

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: Walk me through how a legitimate laptop issuance is supposed to be documented.

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: Normally there’s a service desk ticket for the request, then we prep the unit, and the spreadsheet gets updated when it’s actually issued. For sign-outs we typically have a person physically present and we capture an acknowledgement. When someone just types a name into the sign-out cell, that’s not how it usually looks when the recipient is actually there.

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: What does the spreadsheet currently show for AL-77821?

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: The row shows status “Issued.” In the sign-out area it has “Recipient: Elena Soto” and it lists “Pickup time: 2026-05-13 19:20.” That pickup time is typed text in the cell.

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: Do you recognize Elena Soto?

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: I recognized the name because she’s on the onboarding list, but I haven’t met her in person.

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: Do you have anything showing whether Elena Soto could have legitimately picked up a laptop on 05/13?

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: HR sent an onboarding schedule email. It lists Elena Soto’s start date as 2026-05-20. It also includes a line that says, “Badge pickup: Day 1, 9:00 AM (Lobby).” So she shouldn’t have had a badge or be doing a pickup on 05/13.

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: Who has access to the cage and these records?

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: IT support staff have authorized access. The access-control badges are individual. Also, the building has a credential directory for badge assignments.

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: Did you check the credential directory for the badge involved in the after-hours cage access?

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: Yes. The credential directory entry I saw lists badge ID ending “4421” assigned to Ryan Abad, department “IT Support.”

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: To be clear, your concern with the spreadsheet entry is the “Issued” status and the typed sign-out fields?

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: Yes. Seeing “Issued” with “Recipient: Elena Soto” and a typed pickup time—2026-05-13 19:20—doesn’t match how it usually looks when we hand someone a device. And with her start date being 05/20, it doesn’t make sense as a real pickup on 05/13.

transcript.speaker: DET. WALSH
transcript.text: How did you report the missing device?

transcript.speaker: MAYA LIN
transcript.text: The morning of 05/14 I reported that AL-77821 was missing from Shelf C3 and escalated it to facilities and SPD.

Briefing.subject: Assignment: The Vanishing Laptop (Company IT cage theft)
Briefing.body:
Det. Walsh,

SPD East Precinct opened a theft case after a company-issued laptop (asset tag AL-77821; Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 3) was reported missing from a locked IT cage after hours. The inventory record for that asset shows an “Issued” status with “Recipient: Elena Soto” and a pickup time entered as typed text, and the service desk export shows no corresponding ticket activity for the asset during the relevant period.

Access-control records show an authorized IT-cage badge entry that evening tied to a credential assigned to Ryan Abad (IT Support). Microsoft 365 version history for the IT asset spreadsheet also reflects a save event that night by the user account “rabad,” indicating the inventory record was actively modified around the window of after-hours cage access.

What remains uncertain is the precise chain of custody after the laptop left the cage and whether any additional persons or policy gaps facilitated removal. A separate loading-corridor door contact shows an after-hours door opening during the same general period; facilities on-call coverage (Gavin Holt) overlaps that window, but current information does not establish his entry to the cage or handling of the asset.

This matters now because the report was made the next morning and the documentation trail is already showing potential manipulation (issued entry without workflow support). Immediate investigative objective: lock down and reconcile the access logs, spreadsheet version history, and service desk records to establish an evidentiary timeline for physical access versus administrative changes, and identify the most actionable interview and recovery steps to locate AL-77821 and preserve chain-of-custody.

FollowUpEmails.subject: Missing asset AL-77821 reported from IT Cage / Shelf C3 (morning discovery)
FollowUpEmails.body:
Det. Kendra Walsh,

I’m the IT staffer who reported the missing laptop. At 08:37 on 2026-05-14 I opened the IT cage for morning tasks and noticed the boxed Lenovo ThinkPad T14s Gen 3 with asset tag AL-77821 was not on IT Cage / Shelf C3 where it should have been.

For context: during an end-of-day spot check the prior afternoon (2026-05-13) I visually verified the boxed unit was present on shelf C3.

Also noting our normal issuance workflow: we expect a service desk ticket and a handoff record when a device is issued; a typed name and time entered in the spreadsheet without a ticket is not normal.

—Maya Lin

Explanation: Maya last saw AL-77821 on shelf C3, then after hours someone with IT-cage access removed it and tried to make the spreadsheet show a legitimate issuance. The cage reader logged badge 4421 entering at 19:12, and the credential directory ties that badge to Ryan Abad, placing him at the secure storage during the theft window. Independently, Microsoft 365 version history shows the inventory file was saved at 19:18 by user “rabad,” matching the suspicious typed “Issued / Recipient: Elena Soto / 19:20” entry and indicating deliberate concealment rather than a normal handoff. The decisive contradiction is workflow-based: the service desk search shows no ticket for AL-77821 in the relevant period, so a real issuance wasn’t processed even though the spreadsheet claims it was. The forensic limitation is that access logs and file history prove Ryan’s badge and account activity, not that he physically carried the laptop out—but the combined timing and concealment behavior triangulate him as the only consistent actor. The strongest red herrings collapse: Elena Soto is listed as recipient, yet HR shows she hadn’t started and couldn’t have picked it up, and the LC-2 door opening plus Gavin Holt being on call doesn’t connect him to cage entry or the spreadsheet edit.
